reading.body:
Element Critical CH1 publishes 7 MW of IT capacity across 151,000 square feet of technical space in Wood Dale, Illinois. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 7 MW of IT load is roughly 175 racks, though that assumption is the reader's, not the operator's claim. The footprint is large relative to the power figure, which suggests the campus was built for lower-density, mixed workloads rather than the high-kW-per-rack configurations that modern GPU clusters demand.

PCI DSS certification qualifies the campus to host workloads subject to payment card data standards. HIPAA certification qualifies it to host workloads subject to healthcare data privacy requirements. Neither certification speaks to AI training capability, but together they indicate the campus is oriented toward regulated enterprise workloads where compliance is the primary selection criterion.

Among the 44 Illinois facilities this site has mapped, only 6 publish a megawatt figure, and those 6 sum to 236 MW. CH1's 7 MW ranks fifth among that published group, placing it near the bottom of the disclosed capacity in the state. The state's published total is dominated by larger campuses, and CH1 does not materially shift Illinois's position as an AI infrastructure location. Whether the campus is used for AI inference, enterprise IT, or other regulated computing is not published.
